title: Rocky Mountain National Park Ownership Correction Act
official_summary:
Rocky Mountain National Park Ownership Correction Act

This bill directs the Department of the Interior to convey specified federal land to the owner of specified nonfederal land if the owner of the nonfederal land offers to exchange the land.

The values of the federal and nonfederal land to be exchanged shall be considered to be of equal value.

The nonfederal land that is acquired by Interior shall be administered as part of Rocky Mountain National Park in Colorado.

summary.headline: A 2021 law requires the Interior Department to swap specified federal land for a private owner's land near Rocky Mountain National Park if the owner offers.
summary.what_it_does: The law directs the Department of the Interior to convey specified federal land to the owner of specified nonfederal land, but only if that owner offers to exchange. The two parcels are treated as being of equal value. The nonfederal land Interior receives becomes part of Rocky Mountain National Park in Colorado.

who_it_affects.group: The owner of the specified nonfederal land in Colorado
who_it_affects.how: This owner may trade their land to the federal government in exchange for a specified federal parcel if they choose to offer the swap.

who_it_affects.group: The Department of the Interior and the National Park Service
who_it_affects.how: The department must carry out the exchange if the landowner makes an offer and must manage the acquired land as part of Rocky Mountain National Park.

who_it_affects.group: Visitors to Rocky Mountain National Park
who_it_affects.how: The park's boundaries and managed land would change to include the acquired parcel.

summary.when_it_takes_effect: The law took effect on its enactment date of January 5, 2021, but an exchange happens only if the nonfederal landowner makes an offer; the summary does not give a deadline.
